title: Decoupling The "What" and "Where" With Polar Coordinate Positional Embedding
claim: The standard method encodes content and position jointly through phase; ours separates them by using content only as magnitude, with zero phase.
layout: 2 side-by-side panels, top-down flow from a shared input, matching rotation diagrams below
description: A shared query vector q_t, drawn as a gray bar of six colored squares, sits at the top. Two arrows lead down to two parallel panels. The left panel is labeled RoPE and the arrow is captioned 'Group into 2d components'. Adjacent squares are paired into c=1,2,3 components, and each square holds an orange arrow. Below this, three quadrant sketches show 'Rotate by tθ1/2/3'. In each sketch a black magnitude arrow starts at a green arc (the initial phase) and sweeps through a blue wedge. The right panel is labeled PoPE and the arrow is captioned 'Apply softplus activation'. Each component is a single square holding a horizontal arrow with zero phase. Its three rotation sketches show the same arrow turning through blue wedges. The two sides mirror each other in layout, so the eye compares them directly. Soft pastel colors and gray rounded boxes group the elements.
caption: Illustration compares how RoPE and PoPE encode relative positions via rotations of queries. Left: Three complex-valued RoPE components having magnitudes $\mu_{q_{tc}}$ (black arrows) and initial phases $\phi_{{q}_{tc}}$ (green arcs) are constructed from three pairs of embedding features (orange arrows) of the query vector $\bm{q}_t$ (gray box) at sequence position $t$. These RoPE components are then rotated by angles $t \theta_c$ (blue arcs). Right: Three magnitude components $\mu_{q_{tc}}$ (black arrows) of complex-valued PoPE components are constructed from three embedding features of the query vector $\bm{q}_t$ (gray box) by applying softplus activation. These magnitudes (complex numbers with zero phases) are then rotated by angles $t\theta_c$ (blue arcs). PoPE uses twice the number of components than RoPE as it applies rotations to each component of the query vector $\bm{q}_t$.
abstract: The attention mechanism in a Transformer architecture matches key to query based on both content -- the what -- and position in a sequence -- the where. We present an analysis indicating that what and where are entangled in the popular RoPE rotary position embedding. This entanglement can impair performance particularly when decisions require independent matches on these two factors. We propose an improvement to RoPE, which we call Polar Coordinate Position Embeddings or PoPE, that eliminates the what-where confound. PoPE is far superior on a diagnostic task requiring indexing solely by position or by content. On autoregressive sequence modeling in music, genomic, and natural language domains, Transformers using PoPE as the positional encoding scheme outperform baselines using RoPE with respect to evaluation loss (perplexity) and downstream task performance. On language modeling, these gains persist across model scale, from 124M to 774M parameters. Crucially, PoPE shows strong zero-shot length extrapolation capabilities compared not only to RoPE but even a method designed for extrapolation, YaRN, which requires additional fine tuning and frequency interpolation.
